# Devotional content artifacts

**`manifest.json` and everything under `month/` is generated by
`analysis/export_content.mjs` and rewritten on every build — never hand-edit it.**
This README is the one hand-maintained file here; the exporter leaves it alone.

To author devotional content, see [`content/devotionals/`](../../../content/devotionals/README.md).

```
dist/
  manifest.json      per-month hashes + the content version
  month/01.json      one file per month, every day key present
  …
  month/12.json
```

## Format

Each month file:

```json
{
  "month": 6,
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "days": {
    "06-28": {
      "state": "one",
      "readings": ["Deuteronomy 33-34", "Psalms 119:145-176", "Isaiah 60", "Matthew 8"],
      "devotionals": [
        {
          "id": "11-10-AM",
          "slug": "deuteronomy-33-27",
          "author": "C. H. Spurgeon",
          "sourceWork": "Morning and Evening",
          "reference": "Deuteronomy 33:27",
          "matchedChapter": "Deuteronomy 33",
          "coreText": "…",
          "excerpt": "…",
          "timeHint": null,
          "bodyBlocks": [ … ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Every one of the 365 day keys is present**, including open days
(`"state": "open"`, `"devotionals": []`), so a client lookup never misses.
**There is no `02-29` key** — the leap day clamps to `02-28`.

### The client derives nothing

| Field | Precomputed because |
|---|---|
| `slug` | From the *matched* reference, not the first reference on multi-reference entries. Unique within its day — but **not globally**: 13 slugs recur across different days, so a deep link needs the day key too. |
| `excerpt` | First ~160 chars of the first prose block, cut at a word boundary. |
| array order | Display order, sorted by where `matchedChapter` falls in that day's reading list. **Not** by `timeHint`. |
| `bodyBlocks` | Body already parsed. Three platforms would otherwise each need a markup parser and all three would have to agree. |

`timeHint` is a vestige of the abandoned morning/evening structure and is null
for the large majority. It is carried for provenance and **must not** drive
ordering or presentation.

### `bodyBlocks`

```json
[
  { "type": "p", "spans": [ { "t": "not in one grace only, but in " },
                            { "t": "all", "i": true },
                            { "t": " grace." } ] },
  { "type": "verse", "lines": [ { "indent": 0, "spans": [ { "t": "…" } ] },
                                { "indent": 3, "spans": [ { "t": "…" } ] } ] }
]
```

Two block types, `p` and `verse` — the corpus needs no others. A renderer must
**skip an unknown `type` rather than crash**: authored content may introduce new
ones later.

Verse lines carry `spans` (not plain strings) because some stanzas contain italic
markers, and `indent` because some carry meaningful relative indentation —
hanging continuation lines and centered inscriptions. A renderer that centres the
stanza may ignore `indent`; it exists so the artifact is lossless. This is
verified: reassembling `bodyBlocks` reproduces `bodyPlain` byte-for-byte for all
732 entries, and a mismatch fails the parser build.

## Sizes

| File | Raw | Gzipped | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `month/01.json` | 97 KB | 33 KB | 34% |
| `month/02.json` | 91 KB | 31 KB | 34% |
| `month/03.json` | 124 KB | 41 KB | 33% |
| `month/04.json` | 126 KB | 42 KB | 33% |
| `month/05.json` | 101 KB | 34 KB | 33% |
| `month/06.json` | 111 KB | 37 KB | 33% |
| `month/07.json` | 96 KB | 32 KB | 34% |
| `month/08.json` | 122 KB | 41 KB | 33% |
| `month/09.json` | 106 KB | 36 KB | 34% |
| `month/10.json` | 121 KB | 40 KB | 33% |
| `month/11.json` | 102 KB | 34 KB | 34% |
| `month/12.json` | 124 KB | 41 KB | 33% |
| `manifest.json` | 2.1 KB | 0.7 KB | — |
| **total** | **1321 KB** | **441 KB** | 33% |

Editing one entry refetches one ~35 KB gzipped file, not all twelve — which is why
the manifest carries a hash per month rather than one global hash.

These files are **not** bundled into the mobile app. Bundling all twelve was
measured at +1.46 MB on the iOS Hermes bundle (+24.5%), because Metro inlines JSON
into the bundle; fetching them instead costs +20 KB (+0.32%). The app ships no
devotional content and reads everything from the cache below, so content can be
changed remotely without a new binary.

## Consumption

### Client read path

There is no bundled baseline. The client reads its **cache only**, and fetches a
month on demand when the cache misses. A fresh install therefore has no devotional
until a fetch lands — that is the accepted cost of remote-updatable content.

Rendering never waits on the network: a cache miss resolves immediately to
nothing, and the UI fills in when content arrives. The manifest is cached too,
because without it the device could not know a month's versioned path while
offline.

### R2 sync

```
devotionals/manifest.json                          ← mutable, short TTL (~1 hour)
devotionals/{contentVersion}/month/{MM}.json       ← immutable, long TTL
```

Only `manifest.json` is mutable. **The content version is in the month path**, so
a regeneration writes new objects at new paths and cache invalidation is never
needed — nothing ever has to be purged, and a client holding an old manifest keeps
reading a consistent set of old months.

Sync flow: fetch the manifest, compare each month's `hash` against the cached
hash, fetch only what differs. `contentVersion` is a fingerprint of all twelve
month hashes, so it changes if and only if content changed — a rebuild that
changes nothing produces identical hashes and costs no downloads.

`generatedAt` is `null` in a normal build, because a timestamp would make output
non-deterministic. Inject one for a release if you want provenance:

```bash
DEVOTIONAL_GENERATED_AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" node analysis/export_content.mjs
```

Sync never reads it — staleness is decided purely by content hash.

Shared client logic (manifest parsing, hash comparison, date→day-key with the
leap clamp, day selection) lives in `packages/core/src/devotional/` and is
imported **by subpath**, never through the core barrel, which pulls in Supabase:

```ts
import { devotionalDayKey } from '@gracechords/core/devotional/dayKey'
import { parseManifest, staleMonths } from '@gracechords/core/devotional/manifest'
import { selectDayForDate } from '@gracechords/core/devotional/selection'
```

## Uploading

Manual, by hand. There is no upload script and no credential handling here.

```bash
npx wrangler r2 object put "gracechords-bible/devotionals/$(node -e "process.stdout.write(require('./analysis/out/dist/manifest.json').contentVersion)")/month/01.json" --file analysis/out/dist/month/01.json --content-type application/json --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
```

Repeat per month, then upload the manifest **last** so no client ever sees a
manifest pointing at objects that are not there yet:

```bash
npx wrangler r2 object put gracechords-bible/devotionals/manifest.json --file analysis/out/dist/manifest.json --content-type application/json --cache-control "public, max-age=3600"
```

The bucket is `gracechords-bible` — the same bucket that serves Bible chapter JSON
(`bible/`) and PPTX decks (`pptx/`); `devotionals/` is a new prefix alongside them.

Clients reach it over the custom domain, not the bucket name:
`EXPO_PUBLIC_R2_PUBLIC_URL`, defaulting to `https://assets.gracechords.com`
(see `r2Base()` in `apps/mobile/src/lib/r2.ts`).

## Regenerating

```bash
node analysis/parse_me.mjs         # devotionals.json, incl. bodyBlocks
node analysis/build_schedule.mjs   # schedule.json
node analysis/export_content.mjs   # this directory
```

Deterministic: byte-identical across runs.
